chains.title: How the 1991 crisis built up
steps: 1980s: government spending far exceeds revenue
Borrowing to cover it becomes unsustainable
Imports grow without matching exports
Forex reserves can't pay for even two weeks of imports
India can't repay its foreign borrowings: the balance of payments crisis

chains.title: The rescue and the New Economic Policy
steps: No country or international funder will lend to India
World Bank (IBRD) and IMF lend $7 billion
Conditions: liberalise, open to the private sector, remove trade restrictions
India announces the New Economic Policy (NEP)
Reforms under three heads: liberalisation, privatisation, globalisation

chains.title: Devaluation of the rupee, 1991
steps: The rupee is devalued against foreign currencies
Indian goods get cheaper abroad; imports get dearer
The inflow of foreign exchange increases
It sets the tone for markets to decide exchange rates

chains.title: Why the reforms hurt agriculture
steps: Public investment in farm infrastructure falls
Partial removal of fertiliser subsidy raises costs
Lower import duties, low MSP and no quantitative restrictions
Farmers face international competition
Small farmers like Mahadeva can't cover their costs

chains.title: Box 3.3: the Siricilla tragedy
steps: Power sector reforms end subsidised electricity
Power tariffs rise steeply
Powerloom weavers' wages are tied to cloth output
Power cuts mean wage cuts
A crisis: 50 powerloom workers die by suicide

chains.title: Why industrial growth slowed
steps: Cheaper imports come in
Demand for domestic industrial goods falls
Investment in infrastructure, including power, stays inadequate
Industrial growth slows down
